verdict.line: You lose if the lane stalls past 10 and her Needlework spam/passive sustain take over; you win if you force point-blank trades before she can reset behind Hallowed Mist.

brief.thesis: Volibear vs Gwen is a gap-close check: her whole kit (Q cone, E dash-reset, W untargetability) is built to fight at range or on her terms, while Volibear's Q (Thundering Smash) stun only works if he's already inside 300 range. At 934 games and a 47.4% win rate this is genuinely close — Volibear wins the all-in once he's on top of her, but Gwen's passive sustain and her W's defensive reset mean a Volibear who chases instead of trapping just feeds her healing.

theirWindow.when: Hallowed Mist (18-22s CD) is up when you engage
theirWindow.what: She'll drop Mist the instant your Q (Thundering Smash) lands, going untargetable from outside the cloud. Don't dump your second W (Frenzied Maul) cast or your E (Sky Splitter) into the mist chasing marks — you'll whiff the heal and the slow for nothing.

yourWindow.when: Mist is down and she's in auto range
yourWindow.what: Walk her down immediately. With no defensive reset available she has to trade autos into your stun, so commit Q into double W (Frenzied Maul) right away — the second cast's bonus damage and heal win this exchange outright.

start.why: Carries a 51.6% win rate over 188 games — the sustain and on-hit damage keep you even in extended melee trades where Gwen's passive (A Thousand Cuts) is otherwise chipping you down for free.

boots.why: 52.6% win rate over 196 games. Her entire kit — passive on-hit, Q's center hits, E's on-hit window — is auto-attack damage, so flat reduction hurts her more than magic resist does.

core.why: Leads the highest-winrate path (54.8% over 155 games) and feeds the attack speed that both Lethal Tempo and your passive want for repeated W (Frenzied Maul) resets.
Cooldown refund on crit keeps Q (Thundering Smash) and W cycling faster than Gwen can reset distance with Skip 'n Slash.
Directly answers her passive sustain — every point of healing reduction cuts into the health-percent magic damage she's leeching back off you.

the game goes long and extended skirmishes matter more than single burst trades
she's stacking magic resist and you need the active's sustain and slow to force fights

runes.keystoneWhy: Your passive already grants attack speed on attacks and abilities — Lethal Tempo stacks on top of that and ramps faster than her E's temporary attack speed buff, so extended trades favor you the longer they run.

summoners.why: The 74.4% pick rate and 49.5% win rate reflect the matchup's real pressure point — Ignite burns through her A Thousand Cuts healing on the kill window your Q-stun creates, while Flash guarantees you close the gap she's trying to keep open.

playing.title: Punish her Q dump
playing.detail: Snip Snip! fires up to 6 snips per cast but only resets every 6.5-3.5s. The moment she's finished a full rotation, step in with Q (Thundering Smash) before her cooldown clears.

playing.title: Bait Mist before committing
playing.detail: Don't walk into Hallowed Mist first — that only grants her targeting on you. Wait for her to either drop it on her own or burn its 18-22s cooldown before you engage.

playing.title: All-in the instant Mist is down
playing.detail: With no defensive reset up, land Q into back-to-back W (Frenzied Maul) casts immediately — the second cast's bonus damage and heal win straightforward trades.

playing.title: Slow her off Skip 'n Slash
playing.detail: She's briefly committed to melee range right after the E dash. Drop E (Sky Splitter) on that window so the slow denies the attack-speed buff's value and the cooldown refund.

playing.title: Save R for the kill, not the poke
playing.detail: Stormbringer's cooldown is 160/135/110s before it settles — too valuable at low ranks to use for zoning. Hold it to close a stun-chain all-in, not to interrupt a cone poke.

playing.title: Respect her ultimate scaling late
playing.detail: Needlework's cooldown crashes to 8.5/8s at max rank, letting her poke relentlessly from range in the late game. Push your trades earlier in the lane rather than trying to win a stand-off at level 16+.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win-rate figures are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the matchup reading — why the trades play out this way, and when to commit — is my own tactical judgment layered on top.
